speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With longer life expectancy and healthier life, a senior can continue to work productively and lead a meaningful life for longer.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While longevity touches many aspects of how we live, work and play, I am advocating the need for a concerted focus on work and senior employability.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Enhancing the employability of seniors aged 55 and above is not a new topic in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: There are a myriad of re-employment, retirement and retention policies, financial support and grants to employ seniors, programmes to redesign work, to hire and support seniors who want to continue to work.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The Motion today is to share the voices from surveys and focus group discussions on senior employment and to make recommendations to enable meaningful employment of seniors and the value of the pool of talent for businesses and Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: To understand senior employability, as part of the PAP Seniors Group's effort to reach out and hear the voices of seniors employed and unemployed, we conducted online surveys and focus group discussions with seniors.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This enabled us to learn more about what matters to seniors in their working lives, the opportunities and challenges they face.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In October 2021, PAP Seniors Group started our engagement with seniors aged 50 and above through an online survey.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: To gather further insights, we engaged 200 seniors, including the survey respondents who were willing to participate in Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) to have deeper conversations and dialogues.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In addition, we conducted a literature review on senior employability both locally and globally.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We examined the matter from the perspectives of seniors and various stakeholders, such as employers and younger workers who work with seniors.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Contrary to the popular belief that one would retire, not work and "enjoy" life; seniors we engaged with shared that they want to continue to work as well as to do work that tapped on their capability.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The primary motivation is the sense of satisfaction derived from the contributions made at work, amongst others, of course, more realistically, economic and some sociological motivations.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The survey results corroborated with the qualitative responses of seniors who participated in our focus group discussions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We also conducted online surveys with the younger workers and employers to hear and examine the matter from their perspectives.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In August this year, together with the support of Singapore Human Resources Institute (SHRI) and in partnership with Professor John Wong and the team from NUS and NUHS working on the Singapore Health District @ Queenstown, I joined a dialogue with human resource professionals and decision makers from different companies to understand their experience in hiring and managing seniors in the workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The inputs we gathered from online surveys and FGDs with seniors, employers, younger workers and HR professionals have informed the recommendations I am putting forward on senior employability.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The seniors, employers, HR professionals and younger employees we engaged, acknowledge the value of the many policies and programmes available today, that promote support and advance the hiring, training and retention of seniors in the workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: However, all stakeholders agreed that more needs to be done to address challenges faced and to promote active employment of seniors for more meaningful and happier employment.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It is not just the number of seniors being employed but the quality of the jobs and the work experience of seniors as well as seniors being able to fulfill the requirements of available jobs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Ageism and the continued need to learn new things or skills to stay relevant amid the dynamic macro environment were two key challenges and experiences shared by seniors in the survey and FGDs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Feedback from employers, younger workers and HR professionals highlighted the value of the experience, knowledge and expertise of older workers and the diversity with a multi-generational workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: However again, all stakeholders, including seniors themselves, shared challenges of managing or working in a multi-generational workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In the FGDs with seniors, participants shared their experiences with ageism, with many citing difficulties in getting the opportunity for interviews for the multiple jobs applications made.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In our discussion with HR professionals, they did share that often business leaders may not consider workers above 50yrs for certain roles as they are seen as having not enough "runway".

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While citing these examples, seniors and HR professionals acknowledged that it is often unconscious bias and not a deliberate attempt to discriminate.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: From both the surveys and FGDs, seniors shared that they worry about not being able to continue to work after the retirement and re-employment age.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In Singapore, the Retirement and Re-Employment Act (RRA) protects employees from being dismissed because of age.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: When they reach the retirement age, which is currently 63, the company will have to re-employ them until they reach the re-employment age, which is currently 68.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In the FGD with HR professionals, they highlighted that while the intent is to protect older workers, the RRA is a double-edge sword, leading to an unconscious bias against selecting seniors for roles.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As a company considers hiring someone who is senior and has little "runway" to retirement, they may see it as a risk to hire a person if he/she turns out not be a good fit for the role, as the company will be required to offer re-employment for the person when he/she reaches retirement age.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: From the employer FGD and the online survey with younger workers, a significant proportion of participants highlighted the need for seniors to learn new skills, especially digital skills.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Employers also indicated that seniors may not have the motivation or interest to attend training due to lack of relevance of the training content, or not understanding the language used to deliver training, not being able to follow the pace of training, or not having the time.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And this finding corresponds to the responses by seniors.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The employers also indicated that there is a shortage of manpower to send employees away for training.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I will not give you details of some of the responses they gave.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: These responses translate to the general sentiment that it is beneficial to work alongside older colleagues, but at the same time, one needs to recognise there are challenges in a multi-generational workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: These challenges are attributed to the differences between people in terms of beliefs, mindset, values, disposition and working styles.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I have summarised and shared what we have heard on senior employability from seniors and other stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While we acknowledge and recognise the value of policies and programmes available today that promote, support and advance the hiring, training and retention of seniors in the workforce, the challenges need to be addressed.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We are facing structural economic and social shifts.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We have an ageing population, longevity, healthier life expectancy, declining birth rates, technological advances and disruptions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The traditional one-directional and linear progression of distinct life stages of education, work and retirement and how they affect meaningful employment need to be seen through new lenses.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As people live longer and healthier, we continue to learn, we can be productive and we have a desire to contribute in different ways.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This implies that many of us will continue to work as we age.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This means that we will progress through our life stages in a non-linear way, where there are different pathways.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Just as we allow for different pathways of our young in formal education, perhaps we need to re-think of how we structure this for seniors in the workforce to enable continuous learning and work.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Individuals and employers know the value of continuous learning, the challenge is making time, making time to substantially invest in it.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Hence, the vicious cycle of talent gaps and skills relevancy affecting both businesses and individuals.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For example, to allow a period of perhaps, maybe a few months for work related learning every few years.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Today, there is already significant subsidies and funds available for training and development.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: What is required is to make learning as systemic for workers and not just seniors in the workplace as it is for young in formal education.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Making it systemic does not mean that it is a one size fits all.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Individuals will want to make different choices, choices that will work for them.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: There should be multiple routes connecting the roles, opportunities and commitments of individuals throughout their adult lives.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This will mean that people may transition in and out of life stages, work and learning often.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We need to understand and support individuals to learn, work and age well throughout their lives.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: People need to be able to access learning formal and informal and acquire knowledge in ways that fit their life stages and their abilities.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: An area emphasised by HR professionals in our FGD is the need for functional, technical and cognitive skills to support senior learners prepare and deal with career transitions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We need to recognise that senior learners may face a combination of structural, physical and emotional challenges in learning.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Delivery methods should address the various needs and challenges for positive learning experience and outcomes.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As people live and work longer, work and employment models need to be organised differently to allow greater flexibility for career, parenting, caregiving and personal obligations throughout the different stages of one's life.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Employers, younger workers and HR professionals we engaged, value the experience of the knowledge, experience and expertise of older workers as well as the diversity of a multi-generational workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Opportunities for mentoring and reverse mentoring were also highlighted.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But as I mentioned earlier, the challenges were also highlighted.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With longevity, an ageing population, technological disruptions and flexible work arrangements, people are working longer.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It is not just a matter of young versus old employees but multi-generational, four or five generations.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Many organisations – I do not think we realise this – in many organisations today, there are multi-generations already there.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Therefore, the needs of employees do differ between the different generations: the baby boomers, the Gen X, the Millennials, the Gen Z and now, the Generation Alphas.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Factors such as one's tenure with the organisation, job type, job level add further complexity to this.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Each generation has its preferences, working styles, its strengths, influenced by the world we grew up in, our work experiences and our life stage.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Generational differences can lead to communication and difficulty of working together between different age groups in an organisation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Organisations must give attention to acknowledge and understand the challenges and put the right programmes, tools and processes to support and respect the needs of employees of all ages.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Age diversity in the workplace means varied experiences and points of view, which can become a source of innovation, if we are able to harness the strengths and varied experiences of all workers.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This will not only foster a culture of creative thinking, innovation, better decision making and progress for all but also address the ageism and unconscious biases.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: A multi-generational workforce can also provide a platform for sharing of knowledge through mentoring and reverse mentoring amongst the different generations.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: My recommendation on structural change is broad as I am advocating a rethink of work and learning in the workforce, as people are living longer and healthier lives and are working longer.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It will require all stakeholders to come together and take action to make the change if we are to tap the value of work of seniors and a multi-generational workforce in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: What we do now will affect not only our seniors but our young of today, as they will be seniors of the future.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I think that the Government will play a very important role to put in the reforms in our system to make this change possible and to help galvanise this change, to allow us to make meaningful senior employability possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Indeed, as our seniors lead longer and healthier lives, we need to collectively shift our mindset as a society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is important to see this as a golden opportunity to tap on the accumulated human capital of our seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Government has long placed a strong emphasis on improving the employability of our senior workers and we have made good progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employment rates for senior workers have continued to rise, even during the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is comparable to top OECD countries and reflect the fact that our senior workers are valued by employers in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Perhaps another reality is that we have a tight labour market in Singapore and an ageing workforce, so companies that are progressive and forward looking know that they must tap on the growing pool of senior workers if they want to meet their needs for manpower and talent in the long run.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is heartening to hear that seniors themselves want to continue to work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This will support more senior workers who wish to continue working to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Even as we work towards this goal, we are mindful that there must be sufficient flexibility to avoid unintended consequences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Under the retirement and re-employment framework, the onus is placed on businesses to re-employ senior workers but there is some flexibility to adjust re-employment terms so that businesses can provide employment opportunities to our senior workers while remaining competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: If an employer is unable to identify a suitable position to re-employ the senior worker in, he can provide an Employment Assistance Payment in lieu of re-employment as a last resort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is to help the worker tide over while he or she seeks alternative employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These flexibilities are the outcome of close discussions between tripartite partners and seek to mitigate the concerns on whether re-employment policies may inadvertently disincentivise the hiring of senior workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue to study international best practices and ensure that our retirement and re-employment framework stays robust and relevant for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Beyond just employment, I agree with Ms Jessica Tan that we should also make sure that senior workers are employed in meaningful roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The key to this is reskilling and upskilling our senior workers so that they continue to remain relevant as the economy evolves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Jessica Tan raised an important point that with improving longevity and more frequent economic change, our career paths may no longer be so linear as before but rather, we may need to be prepared for a few career changes throughout our working lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Senior workers, in particular, may wish to or even find themselves needing to transition into new roles or getting into new growth sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For seniors who are currently out of the workforce and require assistance in job search, Workforce Singapore and NTUC's e2i provide career matching services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: There is a career conversion programme, for example, for in-house digital communication professionals, which equips individuals with digital marketing skills to take on in-demand job functions such as brand development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In addition, there are volunteer career advisors, some of them senior workers themselves, who provide their peers with sector- and occupation-specific career advice and mentoring and connect them to relevant Government programmes and services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To complement these moves, we provide structural support through schemes such as the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit, which encourages employers to invest in the training and capability building of their employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Jessica Tan has raised several other pertinent points that can support the upskilling of senior workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will definitely take her feedback into consideration as we continually look into how we can refine our training ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In particular, we are studying how we can support Singaporean mid-career workers in enhancing their skills more substantially during the later stages of their working lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Jessica Tan has also suggested that there must be a culture of continuous learning at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Indeed, this is critical not just for senior workers but also for other workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: While the Government can and will continue to provide the necessary resources and support, employers must also see the value of adopting a "plug-train-play" approach rather than a "plug-and-play" approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is why we have been working with companies to provide quality training to their employees at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have expanded the reach of the National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning (NACE) to uplift the workplace learning capabilities of companies, especially SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To date, more than 1,700 companies have benefited from the programmes offered by NACE.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I agree with Ms Jessica Tan that we must continue promoting different pathways for workers to progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Different businesses will have different needs and so do different senior workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOM has also worked with the Singapore National Employers Federation to develop a structured career planning resource guide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I encourage more employers to utilise this guide and take a more deliberate approach in workforce planning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As our population ages, multi-generational workplaces will increasingly be the norm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As Ms Jessica Tan has pointed out, a multi-generational workforce allows us to harness the experience and expertise of senior workers which can contribute to better productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Senior workers bring a different value-add and complement the younger workerforce as they often have more experience and knowledge of the trade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We all have a role to play in creating effective multi-generational workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Senior workers themselves play an important role in shaping perceptions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It may not be easy but they should be open to job role changes and picking up new skills to keep pace with technological advancements and also changes in the ways of working.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Government will always support our senior workers on this journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers should adopt age-friendly workplace practices such as job redesign to make tasks and workplace environments more age-friendly, providing flexible work arrangements and practising fair employment practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Business leaders and HR have an important role to play in shaping a company culture that is age-friendly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The tripartite partners have taken steps to nurture age-friendly work practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Practices, or TAFEP in short, runs complimentary workshops to guide employers on putting fair employment practices into place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Several Members in this House today and in the past have expressed concerns with ageism affecting job opportunities and career progression for senior workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Government will continue to provide the fullest support to enable our seniors to have longer careers and contribute meaningfully in multi-generational workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We need a strong ecosystem of employers, unions, training institutions and, most of all, employees, young and old, to play a part to enable Singaporeans to harness the benefits of longevity.
